nodes.section_heading: 2. The big breakthrough: HubSpot internal API
nodes.preview:
### Discovery
After Private App token was confirmed unavailable from admin, I cracked HubSpot's internal API by capturing the actual XHR fired when a user changes a property in the UI.

**The endpoint:**
```
PUT https://app-eu1.hubspot.com/api/inbounddb-objects/v1/crm-objects/<objectTypeId>?portalId=139816465&clienttimeout=14000

Headers:
  content-type: application/json
  accept: application/json
  x-hubspot-csrf-hubspotapi: <CSRF_TOKEN>

Body:
[{"objectId": "<contact_id>", "propertyValues": [{"name": "<prop_name>", "value": "<value>"}, ...]}]
```

**Auth:**
- Session cookies from `storage.json` (login-once.js captures them)
- CSRF token from cookie `csrf.app` or `hubspotapi-csrf`

**Object type IDs:**
- `0-1` = Contact
- `0-2` = Company
- `0-3` = Deal
- `0-5` = Ticket
- `0-27` = Task

**Reads** use a different pattern (chirp-frontend-app gateway):
```
POST /api/chirp-frontend-app/v1/gateway/com.hubspot.card.associated.objects.rpc.AssociatedObjectsGatewayRpc/getAssociatedObjectsPaged?portalId=...
Body: { fromObjectTypeId, fromObjectId, toObjectTypeId, propertyNames, sorts, filterGroups, pageLength, offset, ... }
```
Used by `getContactOpenTasks` to enumerate associated tasks.

### Why the discovery took so long
Earlier attempts (DOM clicks, force-click, JS event dispatch) failed because HubSpot's React components don't respond to programmatic clicks — React's synthetic event system needs real-mouse-trajectory hover-then-click.

The fix: in Playwright, do `field.hover()` first, then `field.click()`. The hover triggers the React component to expose its actual edit affordance. Once it's exposed, clicking selects an option, and the resulting XHR is the property-update call.

### What this means going forward
**Any HubSpot write** can now be done via this single endpoint. L

When a link or URL needs to be inspected:

1. **Try `web_extract` first.** It uses HTTP fetch + parse, no Chrome required. Works for 90% of public URLs.
2. **Try `web_search` for context.** If you just need topic/title/summary, search beats fetching.

### Three-step session handshake
1. `POST /mcp` with `{method: "initialize", params: {protocolVersion, capabilities, clientInfo}}` — response includes `Mcp-Session-Id` header
2. `POST /mcp` with `{method: "notifications/initialized"}` + session-id header — gets 202
3. `POST /mcp` with `{method: "tools/call", ...}` + session-id header — actual tool call

Skipping step 1 returns 400 "Missing session ID". Skipping step 2 may also fail.

### Response is SSE-formatted JSON-RPC
Even single-shot tool calls come back as `event: message\ndata: {...}\n\n`. Parse out the `data:` line, then JSON-parse.

### Required Accept header
`Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` — without it, server returns 406 "Not Acceptable".

### Session lifetime
Sessions persist as long as the bridge is up. Cache the session_id in a module global. On 400 "Missing session ID", re-initialize and retry once.

### Schema introspection
Always run `tools/list` once per service to discover real parameter names. The schema may evolve. E.g.: `gmail_send` accepts `html_body` (good for rich emails); `gmail_create_draft` does NOT (plain `body` only).

### MSYS path conversion silently mangles Docker `--build-arg` (and any native-exe arg) starting with `/`

When invoking `docker build` (or any Windows-native `.exe`) from Git Bash on FORGE, MSYS auto-translates POSIX-looking paths into Windows paths. A bare `/` becomes `C:/Program Files/Git/`, `/api` becomes `C:/Program Files/Git/api`, and so on. The conversion is silent — Docker receives the mangled value and bakes it into the image.

**Burned ~1h on Mission Control 2026-05-12.** Rebuilt the FE with `docker build --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=/ ./frontend`. Next.js inlined the value as `"C:/Program Files/Git/"` into the client JS bundle. The login form's `fetch("C:/Program Files/Git/api/v1/users/me")` threw `TypeError` → iPad showed *"Unable to reach backend to validate token"* with no corresponding entry in the backend logs (the request never left Safari).

**Fix:** prefix the command with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`, e.g.

```bash
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 docker build --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=/ -t image:tag ./frontend
```

Alternatives: run from PowerShell/cmd, or use `//` (double-slash escape). `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` is the safest blanket fix.

**To diagnose after the fact:** grep the built artifact (JS bundle, compiled binary, baked container env) for `Program Files/Git`. If it shows up, MSYS got you.

nodes.section_heading: 2. The big breakthrough: HubSpot internal API
nodes.preview:
### Discovery
After Private App token was confirmed unavailable from admin, I cracked HubSpot's internal API by capturing the actual XHR fired when a user changes a property in the UI.

**The endpoint:**
```
PUT https://app-eu1.hubspot.com/api/inbounddb-objects/v1/crm-objects/<objectTypeId>?portalId=139816465&clienttimeout=14000

Headers:
  content-type: application/json
  accept: application/json
  x-hubspot-csrf-hubspotapi: <CSRF_TOKEN>

Body:
[{"objectId": "<contact_id>", "propertyValues": [{"name": "<prop_name>", "value": "<value>"}, ...]}]
```

**Auth:**
- Session cookies from `storage.json` (login-once.js captures them)
- CSRF token from cookie `csrf.app` or `hubspotapi-csrf`

**Object type IDs:**
- `0-1` = Contact
- `0-2` = Company
- `0-3` = Deal
- `0-5` = Ticket
- `0-27` = Task

**Reads** use a different pattern (chirp-frontend-app gateway):
```
POST /api/chirp-frontend-app/v1/gateway/com.hubspot.card.associated.objects.rpc.AssociatedObjectsGatewayRpc/getAssociatedObjectsPaged?portalId=...
Body: { fromObjectTypeId, fromObjectId, toObjectTypeId, propertyNames, sorts, filterGroups, pageLength, offset, ... }
```
Used by `getContactOpenTasks` to enumerate associated tasks.

### Why the discovery took so long
Earlier attempts (DOM clicks, force-click, JS event dispatch) failed because HubSpot's React components don't respond to programmatic clicks — React's synthetic event system needs real-mouse-trajectory hover-then-click.

The fix: in Playwright, do `field.hover()` first, then `field.click()`. The hover triggers the React component to expose its actual edit affordance. Once it's exposed, clicking selects an option, and the resulting XHR is the property-update call.

### What this means going forward
**Any HubSpot write** can now be done via this single endpoint. L
